rationale: Redis cache client wrapper encapsulating connection management, get/set/fetch caching and rate limiting. It is a reusable infrastructure-access component the application depends on, an integration point with the Redis cache, so it is modelled as an application component. Logging is incidental.

A TypeScript interface that only declares named, typed fields (websiteId, date range, unit, timezone) for analytics query parameters. That makes it a data-model object schema. It has no behaviour and no callers in the graph, and it matters only as a minor parameter shape within the analytics query module.

A thin method on the Redis client wrapper that connects, reads a key from the cache and parses the JSON. It is a cache accessor below modelling granularity. The UmamiRedisClient class itself would be the element. It does perform the cache read, so data_persistence is true.

A React module wrapping RevenueMetricsBar with a data-fetching query and a loading panel for board revenue reports. It is a small, file-local UI component: a configured usage of the metrics bar rather than a reusable library component or a routable view. It renders UI and only delegates fetching to hooks.

Factory building the tracker's client-side error collector. It captures exceptions, scrubs them, rate-limits them and POSTs them to the analytics endpoint with retries and 429 backoff. This is error telemetry capture and export to a backend, so it is an observability integration point. It is modelled as the APM error-export pipeline.

A small parsing helper that pulls a client IP from a proxy header value (X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded or a plain value). Its only caller is getIpAddress in the same file. It is an implementation detail of IP resolution, not an architectural element in its own right.

A thin wrapper method on the Redis client class that either soft-deletes a key by setting a DELETED marker or hard-deletes it. It touches the cache, but it is a trivial method of the client component and would not be modelled as an element of its own.

A TypeScript interface declaring only typed fields (session/visit/website ids) for the record route's cache token payload. It is a pure shape declaration, so it is a data-model object schema. It is local to one route file and has no callers, so it is a minor internal unit.

A client-side React Query hook module that fetches sparkline chart data for website, link and pixel lists from internal API endpoints. It is ordinary front-end data-fetching behaviour, a minor internal unit. It calls the app's own API rather than an external system, and it renders no UI itself.

Local TypeScript interface describing props-like shape for a metric card within the WebsiteMetricsBar UI component. It includes a formatter function, making it presentation scaffolding rather than a domain data schema; no callers. Below the granularity a maintainer would name in the architecture model.

A React Query hook that fetches a website's date range from the backend API (/websites/{id}/daterange) and converts the result to Date objects. It is client-side data-fetching behaviour used by a single component, so it is a minor application function. It is not a UI element or an API contract.

A thin wrapper method on the Redis client class that connects and deletes a key. It is an implementation detail of the cache client component rather than an element in its own right, though it does write to durable cache storage.

A small React table component that wraps SharedSharesTable and adds edit and delete action buttons for shares. It is a reusable UI building block with props, which fits a ux librarycomponent. It is a thin wrapper, so its architectural significance is minor.

An exported TypeScript interface that only declares a shape of named, typed fields (a pivoted session-data row), so it is a data-model object schema. It has no callers and is a minor type definition, and it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Thin wrapper method on the Redis client class that serializes a value to JSON and writes it with a TTL. It writes to a cache, so it does touch durable storage, but it is an accessor-level implementation detail of the UmamiRedisClient component rather than an element of its own.

A reusable React form component for creating a share link. It accepts props (createPath, onSave, onCancel) and renders form fields, which makes it a UX library component rather than a routable view. It submits through the useApi hook, so the HTTP integration belongs to that hook. It is a notable but local UI unit.

A TypeScript interface declaring only the shape of the result rows returned by an event-data query (event name, property, data type, value, count). Shape-only declarations are data-model object schemas. It is a minor query-result type that only this file uses, so its significance is low.

A React Query data-fetching hook in the Umami front end. It builds a query key and calls the numeric-series API endpoint, choosing the event-data or session-data path from the source. That makes it internal client application behaviour serving one chart component, best modelled as an application function. It neither renders UI nor reaches external systems itself.

A local event handler inside the TeamDeleteForm component. It invokes a delete mutation, invalidates cache keys and closes the dialog. This is an implementation detail of the UI component rather than a standalone architectural element; the form or its action component would be the modelled element instead.

Private-style lazy connection helper inside the Redis client wrapper; called only by sibling methods. It opens the connection to the external Redis server and logs once, but as a method it is an implementation detail of the UmamiRedisClient component rather than a modelled element.

An exported TypeScript interface declaring only named, typed fields that describe a realtime analytics activity record. Per the charter, a shape-only declaration is a data-model object schema. It is a notable domain type for the realtime feature, but it is passive data with no behaviour or callers recorded.

Next.js route module exposing GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/heatmaps, an HTTP operation contract. It delegates parsing, the permission check (canViewAuthenticatedWebsite) and querying (getHeatmap) to other modules rather than implementing those concerns itself.

A small React utility hook that detects sticky positioning via IntersectionObserver. It is a generic UI helper below the granularity of an architectural element: not a view, component definition or service. It supports UI rendering behaviour, so user_interface is true. It would not be modelled as its own node.

MetricCard is a reusable React UI component with a declared props schema (value, label, tooltip, onClick, footer slot), used across metrics views. It is a library component definition rather than a placed instance or routable view. It is a notable UI building block, not core architecture.

A small local interface describing transient tooltip display state inside a chart component. It is an implementation detail of the chart's rendering, not domain data or a reusable UI contract, so it falls below the granularity an architecture model would record.

A generated SVG icon component (likely produced by SVGR) that only renders a static globe path. It is presentational boilerplate below the granularity of a UX library component a maintainer would name, so it is not an architectural element. It does render UI, so user_interface is true.

A TypeScript interface that only declares a shape (type, limit, offset) used as query parameters for the pageview metrics query. As a pure shape declaration it is a data-model object schema, but it is a minor parameter type that only its query file cares about.

A Prisma query-layer function that issues a paged, searchable read against the pixel collection. It is a named access pattern used by the team and user pixel listing queries, so it is a notable data-access unit rather than a core service.

Post-processing helper that reshapes raw query rows into per-website bucketed chart arrays. It is shared by the ClickHouse and Prisma query variants but does no I/O itself. This is a formatting implementation detail below modelling granularity.

An exported TypeScript interface that declares only a shape (value, total), likely an aggregated property-value count. Shape-only declarations map to data-model objectschema. It is a minor type with no callers, so its significance is low and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

Next.js route module defining GET /api/pixels/charts, an HTTP endpoint contract with a zod-validated query schema. It filters pixel IDs through per-item canViewPixel checks (authorization) and delegates data retrieval to the query layer. This makes it an API operation at the system boundary.

An AES-GCM decryption utility used by secure token parsing. It is a cryptographic protection mechanism, so it fits the security layer, most closely as part of a countermeasure. It is a low-level helper that does not itself verify identity, so its significance is moderate and no concern flag applies.

Exported permission check deciding whether a user may view all teams (admin-only). It is an authorization rule naming one action on one resource, used by the admin teams API route; modelled as a security permission. It is a small but named access rule.

Utility module of date manipulation helpers wrapping date-fns (period parsing, unit functions, formatting). It is a general-purpose helper library rather than a named architectural component, service or data contract. It is minor shared infrastructure that a maintainer would not record as a model element.

A TypeScript interface that only declares the typed argument shape for the saveEventData query function. It is a declared shape, so it is an object schema. It is a minor parameter type local to one query module and has no behaviour of its own.

An exported TypeScript interface that declares only a shape (id, name, slug) for the share rows consumed by a table component. Per the rules, a field-only declaration is a data-model object schema. Its significance is minor: it is a local row type that only the table file uses.

A specific UI button that opens a dialog containing the funnel edit form to add a funnel report. It is a concrete user-operable control that triggers creation, so it fits ActionComponent. It is a small, local UI unit with minor architectural significance.

Module implementing TOTP two-factor authentication: secret generation, otpauth URI, QR code and token verification. It is the MFA mechanism by which principals prove identity, so it is evidence for the security layer's authentication configuration (second factor). It wraps the otplib library locally rather than calling an external system.

A small closure helper inside the tracker that computes a time-bucketed salt string (hourly, daily, weekly or monthly) for anonymization in payloads. It is an implementation detail of getPayload, not a component, contract or telemetry element a maintainer would model on its own.

A TypeScript interface declaring only typed fields (date range, window, steps) as input parameters for the funnel query; per the spec, a shape-only declaration is a data-model ObjectSchema. It is a minor parameter type local to the query module, with no behaviour or storage access of its own.

Formats a ContractCoverage result into a list of error message strings for the OpenAPI document builder. It is a formatting helper in the spec-generation tooling with no behaviour of its own. It is not an architectural element and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

Query module issuing raw SQL against website_event (Prisma/Postgres) and ClickHouse to compute channel metrics. It is an application-issued read operation against a collection, so it fits data-store AccessPattern. It is one of many analytics queries, so significance is notable rather than core.

A props type declaration for a reusable LinkButton UI component. It is part of the component's prop contract rather than an element on its own; the LinkButton library component itself would be the modelled ux element. A props interface is an implementation detail of that component.

Prisma query-layer function that reads one share record by id via findShare. It is a named read access pattern against the share collection, issued by application code and used by the API routes and the auth token parser. It is a thin wrapper, so it has moderate significance.

An exported TypeScript interface that only declares typed fields for a session activity record (event, URL, visit data). It is a pure shape declaration with no behaviour, so it is a data-model object schema. It is a notable domain type but not central to the architecture.

Reusable React chart legend component with a props schema (items, onClick), used by the Chart component. It is a small UI building block, so it is a ux librarycomponent of minor significance. It renders the user interface, but it is not the telemetry itself.

A React button component that opens a modal hosting the segment edit form. It is a concrete user-operable trigger for one specific action (creating or saving a segment), so it maps to a UX action component. It is a minor UI unit.

Although generated, this module is the OpenAPI contract for GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/events/series (getWebsiteEventSeries), declaring its parameters, auth mode and audience. It is the API operation definition itself, a public contract. Auth is only declared as metadata, not enforced here, so no concerns are implemented.

A Next.js page component for the admin team detail route, composing TeamProvider and TeamSettings into a complete screen. It is a routable top-level UI surface, so it is a ux view; it is a thin composition, so it is of moderate significance.

A props interface for the SearchConsoleChart React component. It only declares the component's input parameters and is a typing detail of that component, not a domain data shape or an architectural element of its own. It would at most be captured as attributes of the chart component.

A top-level routable page (Next.js websites/[websiteId]/realtime) that composes the realtime header, chart, log, paths, referrers, countries and world map panels into one screen. It is a UX view and a user-facing feature screen. Data fetching is delegated to a hook.

Props interface for the OtpInput UI component. It is part of the library component's prop schema rather than a standalone architectural element. The OtpInput component itself would be the ux.librarycomponent; its props type is an implementation detail of that definition.

This is a one-line dispatch arrow inside a runQuery map that forwards to clickhouseQuery. It is a trivial wrapper with no logic of its own. The actual access pattern lives in clickhouseQuery, so the dispatcher entry is not an architectural element, and no concern is implemented here directly.

Client-side React Query hooks module that fetches funnel and goal definitions from the backend API. It is internal data-fetching behaviour supporting UI components, so it is a minor application function. It calls the HTTP API, making it an integration point, but it is not itself an API contract or a view.

A props type declaration for a reusable Panel UI component. It belongs to that component's definition rather than standing as an architectural element itself. It is a trivial shape declaration that a maintainer would not name separately from the component.

A trivial React hook that registers and cleans up a document-level click listener. It is a generic UI utility below architectural granularity: it has no domain meaning, no callers, and is not itself a view or component. Its only concern is driving user-interface event handling.

A TypeScript interface that declares only typed fields (date range, attribution model, type, step) used as query parameters for the attribution query. It is a declared shape, so it is an objectschema, but it is a minor parameter type local to one query module.

Next.js route handler for POST /compat/api/reports/revenue, which is one HTTP method-path contract and so an API operation. It performs an inline authorization check via canViewWebsiteSection. Authentication is delegated to parseRequest, and persistence is delegated to the query functions. The route is an externally exposed entry point of a compat reporting endpoint.

A thin React Query hook module that delegates to the generic useAnalyticsQuery with a fixed 'heatmaps' key. It is a minor client-side data-fetching function. It does no persistence or I/O itself, only delegating to the shared hook that does, so no cross-cutting concern applies.

This generated module declares the OpenAPI contract for the /api/share/id/{shareId} path, with deleteShare, getShare and likely more operations, including parameters, responses and auth modes. It is evidence for an API path item grouping those operations. It only declares auth requirements and does not implement any concern itself.

A React props interface for a modal component. It is an implementation detail of the TwoFactorSuccessModal UI component, and it would be captured as attributes of the component rather than as an element of its own. It is not a domain data shape, so it does not qualify as a data-model object schema.

A routable admin page (Next.js app route) that renders the security settings screen, letting an admin toggle the global two-factor requirement. It is a top-level UI surface, so it is a UX view. It delegates the 2FA configuration to API calls through hooks rather than implementing authentication itself.

This exported TypeScript interface only declares a data shape: optional allowFilter and theme fields plus an index signature. That makes it a data-model object schema. It has no callers and is a small parameter type, so its significance is minor. It implements no cross-cutting concern.

Anonymous inline queryFn closure inside a React Query hook that just issues a GET to the session-data-pivot endpoint with assembled params. It is an implementation detail of the hook, not an element on its own. The enclosing hook or the API operation would be modelled instead.

Module defines reusable OpenAPI definitions: the ApiError and Ok schemas plus a registry of standard error responses (400–503) used as components.responses. It is part of the API contract surface, best modelled as the reusable components container. It is notable but not central.

Generated OpenAPI contract declaring the DELETE /api/me/api-keys/{keyId} operation (deleteMyApiKey), with its path parameter, responses and bearer auth. It is direct evidence of an API operation contract. It is generated and only describes the operation, so its significance is moderate. It declares bearer auth but does not itself verify identity.

A small exported error-type interface that extends Error with optional status and code fields, local to a React query hook. It is an implementation detail of error handling, not a domain data shape or contract a maintainer would name architecturally. It has no callers and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Module analyzing coverage of OpenAPI contracts against discovered routes (missing, orphaned, duplicate, path-parameter mismatches). It is build/tooling logic that operates on API contracts rather than being an API contract itself, so it is best modelled as an application function. Notable internal unit, pure computation with no I/O.

A React Query data-fetching hook that wraps a paged GET of /links or /teams/{id}/links for UI components. It is a small client-side application function, one of many similar query hooks. The HTTP call itself is delegated to useApi, so it is only a minor unit.

A top-level admin page component that composes the page header, the add-user action and the users data table into a complete screen under the Next.js app router. It is a routable UI surface, so it is a ux View, and it renders the user interface.

A small structural typing interface that describes the subset of the Prisma client used for raw SQL calls. It is a type-level helper with no callers or behaviour of its own, below the granularity of an architecture element. The persistence work is done by code that uses it, not by this interface.

A generated SVG icon component (likely produced by SVGR) that only renders a static moon path. It is presentational boilerplate below the granularity of a UX library component, so it is not an architectural element. It renders markup, but it is too trivial to count as implementing a user-interface concern.

A TypeScript global declaration augmentation that adds the umami tracker and config properties to the browser Window type. It is ambient typing boilerplate, not an architectural element. The tracker itself would be modelled elsewhere.

Small domain helper that resolves a board's type from its type field or legacy parameters. It is used across board UI components but is a pure derivation utility. It is a minor application function rather than an architectural element, and it implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Query module issuing ad hoc read queries against the website_event collection (Postgres via Prisma and ClickHouse) to compute per-website session chart buckets. It is a named read access pattern in the query layer that reads durable storage, so it belongs in data-store as an accesspattern of moderate significance.
A one-line utility that returns the browser's resolved timezone via the Intl API. It is a trivial date helper with no architectural role, so it would not be recorded as an element in the model.

A small TypeScript interface that declares a field shape (websiteId, resetAt) used as the query-scope parameter for error queries. A declared shape is an object schema. It is minor and file-local, with no callers recorded, so its significance is low.

A trivial props interface that narrows ChartProps with an optional literal 'bubble' type discriminator. It is part of the BubbleChart component's prop contract and is not an architectural element on its own. The library component it belongs to would be the modelled element, not this props declaration.

Query module issuing funnel-analysis reads against Prisma/Postgres and ClickHouse event tables. It is application-issued query code (a named read operation with filter conditions), not stored logic, which makes it a data-store access pattern. It is a notable analytics query rather than a core component.

A React Query hook module that fetches a website's segments from the backend API via useApi. It is client-side data-fetching behaviour, so it fits best as an application function. It is one of many thin, similar query hooks, so its significance is minor. It counts as external integration because it issues an HTTP GET to the backend.

Generated SVG icon component (likely SVGR output) with no logic, callers or behaviour; it is static presentational boilerplate below the granularity of an architectural element, though it does render UI markup.

Exported TypeScript interface that only declares a shape of named, typed fields (name, operator, value, column…), so it is an object schema in the data-model layer. It is a small query-filter descriptor with no callers listed, giving it minor significance.

Query-layer entry point (Umami analytics) that dispatches a goal-stats read to Prisma or ClickHouse. It is a named read operation issued by application code against stored event data, called by several API routes, so it is modelled as a data-store access pattern of moderate significance.

Next.js route module exposing POST /api/auth/sso, an HTTP operation that issues an SSO token for the authenticated user, saving the auth session in Redis and reading the user from the DB. It is an API endpoint implementing authentication token issuance.

A small TypeScript interface that only declares a shape (label, count, percent) for rows rendered by the ListTable component. By the specification's rule, a pure shape declaration is an object schema. It is local to one component's props, so its significance is minor.

PixelSelect is a reusable React select component in Umami's input component set. It is placed in many views and declares its own props. It renders a searchable dropdown of pixels using query hooks. It is a minor UI building block, not a routable view.

A props type for the UserButton component with two optional fields. It is a component-local typing detail, not domain data and not a component definition in its own right. It belongs to the UserButton library component's prop schema rather than standing as a separate architectural element.

Next.js route module defining GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/revenue/sessions: an HTTP operation contract with validated query parameters. It performs an inline permission check (canViewWebsiteSectionRows → unauthorized) and delegates data retrieval to a query function. Authentication is handled by parseRequest, not by this symbol.

Pure string-normalisation utility that compares a request pathname against a configured path, optionally prefixed by a base path. It is used by proxy middleware but is a trivial helper with no architectural identity of its own, below the granularity a maintainer would name.

Next.js route handler for GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/sessions/weekly, an HTTP operation contract with query validation. It delegates the permission check (canViewWebsiteSection), request parsing and the weekly-traffic query to callees, so it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself.

Props interface for a FilterLink UI component. It only types the component's inputs, which makes it an implementation detail of the LibraryComponent rather than an architectural element of its own. At most it would be an attribute of that component's prop schema.

A React Query data-fetching hook module (likely Umami) that wraps a paged GET call to the boards API endpoints. It is client-side application behaviour fetching remote data, a small internal function among many similar query hooks. It calls the backend HTTP API, so it counts as external integration.

A Prisma query function that issues a single write operation, deleteMany on the sessionReplay collection, keyed by websiteId. That is a named access pattern in the data-store query layer. It is a notable but narrow unit of persistence code.

A local TypeScript interface describing the props of one metric card item inside the RevenueMetricsBar component. It is a presentational helper type with no architectural identity of its own and sits below modelling granularity, so it gets no layer or element type.

An inline form-field validation lambda in FunnelEditForm that requires at least two funnel steps. It is a trivial implementation detail inside a UI form, below the granularity of an architectural element.

A thin React Query hook that only delegates to useAnalyticsQuery with a fixed 'heatmaps' key. It is a trivial typed wrapper with no logic of its own, so it sits below the granularity of a model element. The data fetching itself is done by the hook it calls.

A TypeScript interface declaring only named, typed fields (date range and fields list) used as query parameters for the breakdown query. Per the rules, a shape-only declaration is a data-model object schema. It is a minor parameter type, relevant only to its query file, so its significance is low.

A React profile menu button in the app header. It is a user-operable menu control that navigates to settings, admin or logout, so it is a UX action component. Hiding the admin entry with an isAdmin flag is only UI gating, not authorization enforcement. It is a notable but not central UI element.

Next.js route module defining GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/goals/{goalId}/stats, an HTTP endpoint contract. It performs inline authorization checks (canViewWebsiteSection, canViewReport) and delegates data retrieval to query functions. Authentication is handled by parseRequest, and persistence by the query functions it calls.

Local event-handler closure inside the UserSelect component that updates selected username state and forwards the id to the onChange prop. It is an implementation detail of the UI component, not an architectural element on its own. It drives UI state, so user_interface applies.

A React Query hook module that fetches revenue statistics from the backend API for the UI. It is client-side data-fetching behaviour (an application function) rather than a UI view or an API contract. It is notable within the hooks set but is not core. It calls an HTTP endpoint and declares a response shape.

An exported interface declaring only typed fields (filename, function, line, column) for a stack frame, so it is a data-model object schema. It is a small nested shape inside an error schema file and has no callers, so it is a minor unit. It performs no telemetry work itself.

A TypeScript interface that only declares the shape of a breakdown query result row: typed metric fields plus a dynamic index signature. Per the rules, a shape-only declaration is a data-model ObjectSchema. It is a minor result type used locally by the breakdown query module.

A React footer fragment rendered only inside SharePage. It conditionally shows white-label branding. This makes it a non-routable region of a parent view, so it is a subview. It is a minor UI unit of low architectural significance, and it renders UI only.

This is a query-layer module that issues a read against the session_link collection, keyed by websiteId and sessionId, with both Prisma (relational) and ClickHouse variants. It is a named access pattern issued from application code. It is a notable but narrow unit in the query layer.

A TypeScript interface that declares only typed fields (the argument shape for creating a session replay chunk), so it is a data-model object schema. It is a minor input DTO used by the Prisma query layer. It performs no persistence itself.

An exported query function in the queries/sql layer that dispatches to the Prisma or ClickHouse implementation to read a website's event date range. It is a named read operation against storage issued from application code, so it is a data-store access pattern. It is called by the daterange API route.

Thin React Query hook module that fetches paged link shares from the backend API via useApi. It is client-side data-fetching behaviour, a minor unit among many similar query hooks. The HTTP call is delegated to useApi, so the module does not itself implement integration.

A props interface for the RealtimeChart React component. It only declares the component's input shape and is part of the component's definition, so it is not a separate architectural element. The chart component itself would be modelled as a ux librarycomponent.

A reusable React presentational component that renders a colored change indicator with an arrow icon. It declares a props schema and is not tied to any one screen, so it is a UX library component. It is a minor visual building block with little architectural weight.

A React Query data-fetching hook that wraps a GET to /websites/{id}/segments for UI components. It is client-side application behaviour, one of many similar per-resource query hooks. It is a minor internal unit. It delegates the HTTP call to useApi, so it does not perform the external integration itself.

A local event-handler closure inside the LinkDeleteButton component that fires the delete mutation and closes the dialog. It is an implementation detail of the UI component, below the granularity of an architecture element. The containing button would be the modelled ux element, not this handler.

An exported TypeScript interface declaring only typed fields that describe a user's subscription and billing state. Under the specification, a shape-only declaration of this kind is a data-model ObjectSchema. It is a notable domain type for plan entitlements but has no behaviour of its own, and it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself.

React component rendering a UTM breakdown (table plus doughnut chart) for a board/report panel, parameterized by websiteId, param and limit props. It is a reusable, non-routable UI building block with a props contract, so it is modelled as a UX library component. Data fetching is delegated to hooks.

A TypeScript interface that only declares the argument shape for the saveSessionLink query function: named typed fields, no behaviour. It fits an object schema, but as a parameter type for one query it matters only within its file.

Generated SVG icon component (SVGR-style) with no logic, props schema, or callers. It renders a static money glyph and is asset boilerplate below the granularity of a UX library component element. It does render UI, but it is not architecturally meaningful on its own.

A React props interface for the Attribution report component. It only declares the component's input parameters, which is boilerplate attached to the UI component rather than a standalone architectural element. At most it would be an attribute of the ux view, not its own node.

Next.js route handler for DELETE /api/websites/{websiteId}/funnels/{funnelId}, so it is an API operation contract. It delegates authentication to parseRequest, the permission check to canDeleteReport and deletion to deleteReport. It orchestrates these calls but implements none of the concerns itself.

A SQL-fragment builder that produces a ClickHouse CASE expression grouping referrer domains. It is a string-formatting helper used only by clickhouseQuery in the same file. It does not execute queries or touch storage itself, so it sits below architectural granularity.

An exported TypeScript interface that only declares a shape with two numeric fields (startAt, endAt). Per the spec, field-only declarations are data-model object schemas. It is a small value type with no callers recorded, so it has minor significance and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Reusable common React component that wraps children in an error boundary, renders an error fallback UI with a reset button, and logs errors to the console. It is a shared UI building block, so it maps to a ux library component. Its console logging is minor observability. Notable but not core.

Inner render helper of the WebsiteSelect component that formats the selected-value display (icon plus truncated text). It is a private presentational detail of a UI component, not an architectural element itself, though it does render user-facing UI.

React confirmation form for leaving a team. It is a non-routable UI fragment that composes the shared ConfirmationForm and sends a DELETE request to the team-membership API. It is a notable UI unit in the teams area but not a standalone routable view, so it is modelled as a subview.

Generated OpenAPI contract that defines the GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/session-data/property-series operation, including its parameters, auth mode and tags. Its content is an API operation contract. It is generated, which tempers significance, but it remains the documented endpoint contract. The auth field only declares a scheme and does not verify identity.

ClickHouse-specific implementation of the retention cohort query: an ad hoc SQL read against the website_event collection, issued from application code via rawQuery. This matches an access pattern in the data-store layer. It is a notable query variant, but it sits behind the getRetention dispatcher.

An exported TypeScript interface that declares only the typed fields of a query result row (eventName, propertyName, dataType, total). A shape-only declaration is a data-model object schema. It is a minor result type local to one query module, so its significance is low.

A props type declaration for the FilterButtons UI component. It is an implementation detail of that component's prop schema, which would be an attribute of the ux librarycomponent rather than an element in its own right. It is not domain data, so it is not a data-model object schema.

A one-field options interface (optional chunkIndex) that parameterises a heatmap extraction query function. It is an implementation detail of the function's signature, not a domain data shape or contract a maintainer would name, so it is not an architectural element.

React UI component that renders the events table on the website events page. It configures a DataTable library component with specific columns (event, session, location, browser, device, created), so it is an application-specific configured usage of a table component within the events view. Notable UI unit, but not core architecture.

React hook that returns a static, localized catalogue of filterable analytics dimensions (path, referrer, country, utm, etc.) with group labels. It is used by report and filter components. It is a configuration/data helper with no rendering or I/O of its own: a minor internal application function.

An anonymous arrow function in a database-dispatch map that only forwards to relationalQuery. It is a trivial dispatch wrapper. The real persistence work happens in the callee, so this entry is not an architectural element in its own right.

A one-line setter that updates the timezone field in a client-side state store. It is a trivial accessor with no logic of its own and no persistence. It sits below the granularity a maintainer would name, so it is not an architectural element; the app store module itself would be the modelled element.

TypeScript interface declaring only the shape of a cached collection-session token payload (website, session, visit IDs, issued-at). It is a pure field declaration, so it models as a data-model object schema. It is minor and has no callers listed.

Next.js route module defining POST /api/2fa/setup/initiate, an HTTP operation that initiates TOTP two-factor setup. It generates and encrypts the secret, then upserts it via Prisma. This is an authentication-related endpoint and a security boundary, so it is significant.

A tiny internal type holding the summary and description text used to annotate OpenAPI operations. It is documentation metadata scaffolding with no callers and is not an architectural element on its own. At most it is an attribute of api.operation elements.

Small React Query hook module that fetches the paged admin teams list from the backend /admin/teams endpoint via useApi. It is a client-side data-fetching function, one of many similar query hooks, so it is a minor internal application function rather than an API contract or UI view.

NavMenu is a reusable UI component in components/common. It takes a props schema (items, title, selectedKey, onItemClick) and is reused by AdminNav and WebsiteExpandedMenu. It renders grouped navigation links, so it is a library component definition rather than a route table or a specific view. It is a notable shared building block.

Utility module that resolves the client IP from proxy headers, using trusted-proxy CIDR configuration and RFC 7239 Forwarded parsing. It is a notable internal capability for analytics geolocation and for resisting spoofing, but it is a library function group, not a service or API surface. It implements none of the listed cross-cutting concerns itself.

A small internal type holding transient tooltip display state (title, color, value) inside the BarChart component. It is an implementation detail of the chart's rendering, not domain data or a reusable UI element, so it falls below the architectural granularity threshold.

Trivial accessor returning a constant error message for misconfigured two-factor crypto. Although used by many 2FA routes, it performs no authentication work itself; it is an implementation detail below modelling granularity.

A TypeScript interface declaring only the shape of a query result row (x, t, y) for event stats. It is a pure declared shape, so it is a data-model object schema. It is a minor result type used only within this query file.

Prisma query module providing CRUD and paged lookups against the teamUser table: a repository/DAO layer issuing read/write operations to one collection. That makes it data-store access patterns. It is notable for team membership but is not itself a central abstraction.

A ClickHouse-specific query issued from application code that counts event_data rows per website within a date range. It is a named read access pattern against the event_data collection, part of a dual-backend query module, so it is a notable but not central unit.

A concrete UI button that opens a clone-board dialog and navigates to the design page after saving. It is a user-operable trigger, so it is an ActionComponent. It hides itself for view-only users, which is a role-based UI access check. It is a notable but local UI unit.

A props type declaration for the WebsiteDateFilter React component. Props of a component are attributes of its LibraryComponent element (the props schema), not a separate architectural element. It is boilerplate typing below modelling granularity.

A props interface for the MetricsBar UI component. It is part of that component's prop schema, which would be an attribute of the ux.librarycomponent element rather than a separate element. On its own it is boilerplate type scaffolding with no callers.

A client-side React Query hook (Umami) that fetches paged website sessions from the backend API through useApi. It is a small data-fetching function among many similar query hooks, so it is minor application behaviour and not a UI view or API contract. It calls the HTTP client rather than implementing integration itself.

An inner handler of the two-factor login page. It submits the partial token with an OTP or backup code, stores the resulting auth token and user, handles lockout, and navigates afterwards. Its core work is identity verification (the second factor), so it is evidence for the security authentication mechanism, not a standalone UI element.

A small React button component that renders a link to the pixel edit route. It is a concrete user-operable control that triggers navigation, so it is a UX action component. It is a minor UI unit of low architectural significance.

A reusable React component rendering a filter dialog button. It is used by the website, link and pixel control panels and serialises the chosen filters into URL params. It is a UI building block reused across several views, so it is modelled as a ux library component of moderate significance.

Small exported mutator on a client-side Zustand-style replays store. It resets in-memory state when the website and source match. This is internal application behaviour used by two replay tables. It is not durable persistence and not UI rendering. Minor significance.

Generated SVG icon component (SVGR-style) wrapping a static path; pure presentational asset with no props schema, logic or callers. It is boilerplate below the granularity of an architecture model, though it does render UI.

A tiny React hook that derives isMobile/isPhone flags from the current breakpoint. It is a responsive-layout utility used widely by UI components, but it is a trivial helper below architectural granularity rather than a view, component or service. It supports UI rendering decisions.

A small internal TypeScript interface that bundles SQL join and filter fragments with query parameters for building a heatmap query. It is a query-construction helper type, not domain data or a contract, and sits below the granularity of an architectural element. It does no persistence work itself.

A tiny props interface extending ChartProps with one optional 'type' field. It is part of the PieChart library component's prop schema rather than an element in its own right, and it is too fine-grained to model separately. It declares a shape but renders nothing, so no concerns apply.

A header region of the Teams page that composes a PageHeader with join and add buttons. It is a non-routable fragment of the Teams view, so it is a subview. It performs a light role check that hides the add button for view-only users, which is UI-level authorization gating.

DataGrid is a reusable common UI component with a declared props schema (query, search, paging, render slots) used across many views. That makes it a library component in the UX layer. It renders the interface, so user_interface is true. Its localStorage write only stores a display-mode preference, which does not count as durable data persistence.

A Prisma query helper that issues a findMany on the share collection, keyed by entityId, and returns the latest share slug for each website. It is a read access pattern in the query layer, and its only caller is getWebsites. It is a minor enrichment step, not a standalone service.

A small TypeScript interface that only declares a shape (a schema plus an optional flag) used inside the source-analysis module. A shape-only declaration is a data-model object schema. It is a minor internal structure that matters only to its own file, so significance is low.

Next.js route module defining GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/revenue/metrics. It validates query params with zod, performs a permission check (canViewWebsiteSection) and returns revenue metrics. This is an HTTP API operation contract, so it is a significant API endpoint. Authorization is checked inline; persistence is delegated to the query layer.

An inline arrow-function accessor in a metric formatting config, used to compute ROAS by dividing conversion value by cost. It is a trivial derivation helper for display formatting and not an architecturally meaningful element.

A TypeScript interface declaring only typed fields (property, operator, value) for a funnel step filter used by the funnel query module. It is a pure shape declaration, so it maps to a data-model object schema. It is a minor internal type with no behaviour of its own.

An exported interface that only declares a shape: optional release, environment, tags and fingerprint fields passed when capturing an error in the tracker. A pure field declaration is an object schema. It is a small options bag with no callers and performs no telemetry work itself, so significance is low and no concern applies.

An inline React Query queryFn arrow function inside the ErrorShared component that delegates to the useApi get helper. It is a one-line implementation detail of the component's data fetching, not an architectural element on its own.

A recursive helper that sorts JSON object keys for deterministic serialization. It is a formatting utility called only by serializeOpenApiDocument, so it is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

An exported TypeScript interface that only declares the shape of a revenue metrics query result: arrays of name/value breakdowns by country, region, referrer and channel. A pure field declaration is an object schema. It is a minor result type local to the query module.

Generated OpenAPI contract declaring the GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/revenue/metrics operation: its operationId, parameters, auth mode and responses. Although generated, it is the API contract for one method-path pair, so it is evidence for an api.operation. It declares auth requirements but does not implement them, so no concern flags apply.

Prisma query module for the board table, providing CRUD and paged/filtered lookups by user or team. It is repository/DAO code issuing access patterns against one collection, so it belongs to the data-store layer. It is a notable but ordinary persistence unit.

A TypeScript interface declaring only typed fields (websiteId, x, y) for query result rows. Per the spec, shape-only declarations are data-model object schemas. It is a minor result type local to one query file, so significance is low.

Private helper nested in the attribution query module. It returns a SQL CTE fragment (first-click vs last-click) used by clickhouseQuery and relationalQuery. It builds query text but executes nothing itself, so it is an implementation detail of the attribution access pattern rather than an element of its own.

A trivial formatting helper inside a React hook. It maps a locale code to a display language name through a lookup table. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity, so it is not a modelled element and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A small options parameter type for a single query function, declaring two optional filter fields. It is an implementation detail of the query's signature, not a domain data shape or a contract worth modelling on its own. It performs no persistence itself.

Next.js App Router page file: it binds the URL pattern /admin/teams/[teamId] to the AdminTeamPage view, passing the route parameter and setting the page title metadata. That makes it a client-side route entry, not the view itself, which lives in AdminTeamPage.

A React Query hook module that fetches revenue chart data from the backend API (/websites/{id}/revenue/chart) with date and filter parameters. It is client-side data-fetching behaviour that the UI consumes, so it is an application function of moderate significance, and it performs the HTTP integration itself.

This is a type-declaration augmentation (.d.ts) for a third-party UI library's Select props, adding only an optional children field. It is typing boilerplate for an external component rather than an architectural element, with no callers or behaviour, so it is not modelled.

A UI button on the security settings page. Activating it opens a modal containing the password edit form and shows a toast on save. It is a concrete user-operable trigger, so it is modelled as an action component. The credential handling itself happens in PasswordEditForm, not in this symbol.

This is a React component props interface for PageviewsChart. It is part of that component's prop contract rather than an element in its own right. The prop schema would be an attribute of the ux library component, so it is not modelled separately and is minor.

A one-line i18n helper inside a React hook that prefixes a message id and calls the translation function. It is a trivial formatting and lookup utility with no architectural standing of its own, so it is not modelled as an element.

React form component that renders the team-join access-code form inside a modal opened by TeamsJoinButton. It is a non-routable UI fragment with a submit action calling the /teams/join API through a hook. It is a notable UX element but not a routable view.

React component in Umami's compare page that renders comparison metrics tables with a view selector. It is a UI region embedded within the compare page view, not routable itself, so it is modelled as a UX subview. It is notable within the compare feature.

An anonymous arrow function used as a dispatch-map entry that only forwards to relationalQuery for the Prisma backend. It is trivial routing boilerplate. The real data-store access pattern lives in relationalQuery and the enclosing query function, so this entry has no architectural meaning of its own.

A React component props interface for the Funnel report component. It is an implementation detail of the UI component's contract, not an independently modelled element. The Funnel component itself would be the UX element, so these props are not one in their own right.

A React form component for joining a team via access code. It renders UI and submits to the /teams/join API through a hook. It is a non-routable form fragment embedded in a modal or page, so it is modelled as a UX sub-view of moderate significance.

Next.js route handler for GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/event-data/properties, which makes it an HTTP API operation contract. It validates query parameters, delegates the permission check to canViewWebsiteSection, and delegates the data fetch to a query function. Because it only calls the code that does that work, no concern flags are set.

Configuration contract for a session recorder: it sets whether replay and heatmap capture are enabled, their sampling rates, masking level and blocked selectors. That is a setting for how user-session telemetry is instrumented, not domain data, so it fits apm InstrumentationConfig. It is a notable but non-central unit.

An exported TypeScript interface that declares only a shape: name, filterLabel, label and group. Under the spec it is an object schema. It is a small UI-side field descriptor used by a hook, so its significance is minor.

Generated OpenAPI contract declaring GET /api/links/charts, with its query parameters, responses and bearer-or-share auth. Although generated, it is the API contract for one endpoint, so it is evidence for an api operation. It only declares auth and does not implement any cross-cutting concern itself.

A routable settings page under the Next.js app directory that composes the page header, panel and preference settings components into one complete screen. That makes it a UX view. It is a notable but ordinary page, not a core architectural element.

A React props interface for the Journey report component. It only types the component's inputs and is part of the Journey view's prop contract. It is not a separate architectural element; it would be captured as attributes of the UX component rather than as a node of its own.

Next.js route module exposing GET /p/[slug], a tracking-pixel endpoint for external embedding. It looks up the pixel via a Redis cache or Prisma, forwards an event to the send API, and returns a 1x1 GIF. This makes it an HTTP operation and an ingestion integration point; it reads the cache and database directly.

Shared Next.js route handler for the /mcp endpoint, invoked by the GET, POST and DELETE exports. It gates on a feature flag, delegates authentication to authenticateMcpRequest, and serves the MCP server transport to external clients. It is the HTTP entry point of the MCP integration boundary, so it is modelled as an API operation.

React client component that renders a bar chart and metric cards of numeric property sums and averages, using query hooks. It is a reusable UI building block embedded in property-data views, so it is a UX library component of moderate significance. Data fetching is delegated to hooks.

A TypeScript interface that declares only a shape: query filter parameters for the heatmap query, extending QueryFilters. By the charter, a field-only declaration is an object schema. It is a minor parameter type used only within its query file, so its significance is low.

Access-check function that decides whether an identity may view a report. It permits admins and owners (subject to billing access) and otherwise falls back to website or section permissions. This is a condition-plus-permit/deny evaluation unit enforced by several API routes, so it is modelled as a security policy rule implementing authorization.

Next.js route module defining GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/stats, an HTTP endpoint contract returning website stats with a comparison period. It delegates parsing and auth to parseRequest, the permission check to canViewWebsiteSection and data access to getWebsiteStats, so it implements none of those concerns itself.

A small React control inside the heatmap report view. It configures a library Select to choose the screen-width bucket, and the click and scroll heatmap views each place it. It is a minor UI fragment local to its file, below the level of a reusable library component or a view.

A type-declaration augmentation in a .d.ts file that adds a children prop to a third-party Tooltip component's props. It is typing boilerplate for an external library, not a component definition, schema or architectural element. It has no callers and is not something a maintainer would name when explaining the system.

An exported TypeScript interface that only declares a data shape (dimension plus rows) for the Search Console query hook's response. Under the charter, a declared shape is an objectschema. It is a minor response type that matters mainly to its own hook file.

Next.js route module defining a POST HTTP handler for the compat UTM report endpoint. It is an API operation contract: it parses and validates the request, enforces a permission check via canViewWebsiteSection with an unauthorized response, and delegates data retrieval to the query layer. Authorization is performed inline, while persistence is delegated.

A React hook that derives analytics filter parameters from URL query state and share settings. It is widely reused (34 callers) by query hooks, so it is a notable internal function. It is not itself a UI view, route or API contract.

Module of chart label formatting and bucket-index helper functions. These are pure formatting utilities that sit below architectural granularity, and nothing calls into the module as a named component. They are not a UI component and implement no cross-cutting concern.

A React props interface for the MetricLabel UI component. It is a boilerplate prop typing that belongs to the component definition and is not a standalone architectural element. The component itself, not its props interface, would be modelled in the ux layer.

A Next.js route handler for GET /api/teams/{teamId}/users/{userId} is an API operation. It performs an inline authorization gate: it calls canUpdateTeam and returns unauthorized. Authentication and persistence are delegated to parseRequest and getTeamUser, so those concerns stay false. It is a significant endpoint contract.

A Next.js route module that groups the GET, POST and DELETE handlers for /api/websites/{websiteId}/annotations/{annotationId}, so it is modelled as a PathItem at the HTTP API boundary. It performs permission checks inline (canUpdateWebsite, canViewSharedWebsiteFilters) before acting. Authentication is delegated to parseRequest and persistence to the query layer.

An anonymous inline queryFn lambda inside a React Query hook. It builds request parameters and calls the API client's get for event- or session-data values. It is an implementation detail of the enclosing hook, not an architectural element in its own right.

A small parameter-bag interface (type, limit, offset) for a single query function. It is an implementation detail of the query's signature rather than a domain data shape a maintainer would model, so it is below element granularity.

A React UI fragment on the preferences settings page that renders a searchable timezone select plus a reset button. It is non-routable and composed into a parent settings view, so it is modelled as a subview. Persistence is delegated to the useTimezone hook, so the symbol itself does none.

A one-line setter that writes the user into the client-side app store's in-memory state. It is a trivial accessor on the store and not an architectural element on its own. Several login and logout flows call it, but it neither verifies identity nor persists anything durably.

An exported TypeScript interface declaring only typed fields for shared-dashboard data (share id, slug, type, target ids, parameters, token, white-label settings). It is a pure shape declaration, so it is a data-model object schema. It is notable within the share feature but is not a central contract.

An exported TypeScript interface that only declares the shape of the session stats query result: named numeric fields with no behaviour. Per the spec, a shape-only declaration is a data-model object schema. It is a minor result type that matters mainly to its query file.

Although generated, this module declares the OpenAPI operation contract for GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/replays, with its parameters, auth mode and audience. That is an API-layer Operation element. It only declares the bearer-or-share auth requirement and does not implement authentication, so no concerns are flagged.

Small utility module that normalizes pathnames and compares them against a configured path with an optional base path. It is a string-matching helper with no callers recorded and no architectural role of its own, so it falls below the modelling granularity.

A local UI event handler inside the BoardEditRow component. It appends a column to the board's row layout through an immutable update and then calls updateBoard. It is an implementation detail of the component rather than an architectural element. It responds to user interaction in the UI, but does not itself write to storage.

A one-line inline error callback that forwards an event to a debug log within the MCP route configuration. It is a trivial logging hook, an implementation detail rather than a nameable architectural element, even though it does perform logging. The large caller count is likely a name-resolution artifact.

A props type for a small presentational IconLabel component. It is an implementation detail of the component's prop contract, not domain data and not a UI element on its own. The IconLabel component itself would be the modelled library component, so this interface is not separately recorded.

A one-field parameter interface (optional limit) for a single query function. It is a trivial typing helper, too small and too local to be a named architectural element, so it would not be modelled as an object schema. No callers, no cross-cutting work.

React modal component presenting a session profile as a standalone dialog surface, opened through a URL query param and closed by router replace. A modal screen fits ux view. It is a notable UI unit within the sessions area, but only moderately significant.

This is the props interface of the reusable DataGrid library component, declaring its prop schema and render slots. It is part of the DataGrid component's contract rather than a standalone element, so its significance is low. It is mapped to ux librarycomponent.

A React component that renders a session-replay player by embedding rrweb-player and sizing it responsively. It is not a routable page: it is used by ReplayPlayback. That makes it a reusable UI component definition within the replay view, a notable unit of the replay feature's UI.

A query-layer module that composes the performance chart and stats queries into one result for the legacy report endpoint. It issues no storage access itself; it combines two queries in parallel, so it is an internal application function of moderate significance rather than a data-store access pattern.
A trivial numeric clamp utility in a colors helper file, with no callers or architectural role. It is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture model element.

A React module that renders the shares table inside the website settings page, along with edit and delete dialogs. It is a non-routable region of the settings view that composes the shared table, action buttons and modals. Persistence happens indirectly through the useDeleteQuery hook, so data_persistence is false.

A React props interface for the GoogleAdsChart component. It only declares the component's input shape and is an implementation detail of that UI component, not an architectural element on its own. Any props schema would be captured as an attribute of the component rather than modelled as a separate element.

Next.js route module defining GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/session-data/stats. It validates query parameters, performs a permission check via canViewWebsiteSection and returns session-data activity stats. It is an HTTP endpoint contract, so it is an api operation. Authorization is enforced inline; authentication and persistence are delegated to parseRequest and the query layer.

Next.js route module defining POST /api/reports/funnel (compat) handler: an HTTP endpoint contract. It delegates auth parsing, the permission check (canViewWebsiteSection) and the query (getFunnel) to other modules, so it does not itself implement those concerns. It is an API operation and an integration point for funnel reports.

A TypeScript interface declaring only the field shape of the board-clone form's values (name, description, type, entityId). Per the rules, a declared shape is an object schema, but it is local to one form component and minor.

A trivial inline render callback inside SegmentsDataTable that only returns a SegmentAddButton element. It is an implementation detail of the table component, not an architectural element. It does render UI, so the user_interface concern applies.

Module declares the OpenAPI contract for GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/utm/metrics (operationId getWebsiteUtmMetrics) with parameters, responses and auth mode. It is an API operation definition, a public contract element. It declares an auth requirement but does not itself verify identity or enforce permissions.

A React props interface for the Heatmap component. It is a typing detail of the component's prop contract rather than a standalone architectural element. The Heatmap view or component would be modelled in the ux layer, and this interface would at most be an attribute of it.

Thin React Query hook module fetching board shares from the backend API via useApi. It is client-side data-fetching behaviour, so it is a minor application function. It is one of many similar query hooks and has low individual architectural significance.

A React Query data-fetching hook (Umami-style) that calls backend array-series endpoints for event or session property data. It is client-side application behaviour used by PropertyChart, which makes it an internal application function. Its HTTP call to the API justifies external_integration. It is a notable but ordinary unit.

A React props interface declaring two callbacks (onClose, onSuccess) for the TwoFactorDisableModal component. It is component-local typing boilerplate rather than a domain data shape or an architectural element. Any modelling would happen on the modal view itself, so it gets no layer.

A UI fragment in the admin websites page that combines a DataGrid (with search) and the AdminWebsitesTable, fed by the websites query hook. It is a non-routable region of an admin view rather than a screen of its own, so it is modelled as a ux subview of moderate significance.

A React props interface for the GoogleAdsConversionsTable component. It only declares the component's input parameters, which is an implementation detail of that UI component rather than a standalone architectural element. If modelled at all, it would be an attribute of the component, not a node.

Next.js route handler for GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/revenue/chart, an HTTP operation contract. It validates query params, enforces an access check via canViewWebsiteSection, and delegates the data query to getRevenueChart. Authentication is handled inside parseRequest, so it is not counted here, while the authorization gate is performed in this handler.

A trivial response-formatting helper that builds a 503 JSON error body. Route handlers reuse it, but it is boilerplate below the granularity of an architectural element and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Next.js route module exposing GET and POST on /api/websites/{websiteId}/segments, i.e. one path with two operations, so it is an API path item. It performs inline permission checks (canViewSharedWebsiteFilters, canUpdateWebsite) and validates request bodies. Persistence is delegated to the prisma query functions rather than done here.

A TypeScript interface that only declares the shape of a board component's configuration field descriptor (name, label, type, options, defaults). By the charter it is an object schema. It is a minor supporting type used within the board component registry and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A React Query hook module that fetches revenue metrics from the backend API endpoint for a website. It is client-side data-fetching behaviour used by UI components: a minor application function, one of many similar query hooks. It calls an HTTP API, so it counts as external integration.

A small inner event handler inside the FieldSelectForm React component. It forwards the selected fields to the onChange callback and closes the form. This is a trivial UI callback, an implementation detail of the component rather than an architectural element. It does drive the user interface.

A React props interface for the FilterRecord component. It is part of the component's prop contract rather than an architectural element of its own; the FilterRecord library component would be modelled instead. Treated as an implementation detail of the UI component.

Inner render callback inside the DateFilter component that chooses between a DateDisplay and the default children. It is a trivial presentation helper and an implementation detail of the component, not an architectural element on its own. It does render UI.

An exported TypeScript interface that only declares the shape of event metric query result rows (x, t, y), making it a data-model object schema. It is a small result type used within one query module, so it has low architectural significance.

Umami query module that upserts flattened session data into the session_data table (Prisma/SQL) or sends it to ClickHouse/Kafka. It is a named write operation issued by application code against one collection, which makes it a data-store access pattern. It writes durable storage directly.

A local helper inside the WorldMap component that computes a country's fill colour from its metric value and the current theme. It is presentation formatting logic below the granularity of an architectural element. It only supports UI rendering.

The module is a Next.js route file that defines the GET and POST operations on /api/websites/{websiteId}/replays/saved/{replayId}, so it maps to an API path item. It enforces access with per-website permission checks. Identity parsing and persistence are delegated to helper and query modules, so those concerns are not set.

A small options bag for a query function: two boolean flags controlling whether the password is included and whether deleted users are shown. It is a parameter type for one internal helper, not a domain data shape or contract a maintainer would model as an element.

A small React fragment, rendered only inside the SearchConsoleReport view, that shows an empty-state panel explaining a setup problem plus a button linking to integrations. It is a non-routable UI region of one parent view, so it is a subview, but it is minor and of interest mainly to its own file.

Generated OpenAPI contract module defining the GET /api/auth/subscription operation (getSubscription) with its parameters and responses. Though generated, it is the API contract evidence for one operation, so it is modelled as an api operation. It declares auth metadata but does not itself verify identity.

A small options interface for a React query hook (replay query parameters: until, chunkIndex, eventIndex). It is a hook-local parameter bag, not a domain entity or API contract, so it falls below the granularity a maintainer would name in an architecture model.

Props interface for a Badge UI component. It is an implementation detail of the library component's prop schema rather than a standalone architectural element. The Badge component itself would be modelled as ux.librarycomponent; its props type is captured as attributes of that component.

Module declaring the OpenAPI contract for GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/heatmaps (operationId getWebsiteHeatmaps), with parameters, a response schema and bearer auth metadata. It is an API operation definition, an architecturally significant contract. It declares auth but does not itself enforce it.

A React Query data-fetching hook that calls the internal revenue metrics API endpoint for a website, using date and filter parameters. It is client-side application behaviour supporting the revenue report view. It is a notable internal unit rather than a UI element or API contract. HTTP to its own backend is not an external integration.

React component that composes metric panels (sources, environment, map, location) inside the pixel detail page. It is a non-routable region of the pixel view, grouping several component instances, so it is a ux subview of notable but not central significance.

A one-line wrapper that stores the auth token in client storage under a constant key. It is called by the login, two-factor, SSO and password flows, but it is a trivial helper below the granularity of an architectural element. It does touch token handling and persistence.

A TypeScript interface declaring only named, typed fields that describe the result shape of OpenAPI contract coverage analysis (discovered, missing and orphaned operations). It is a pure shape declaration, so it is a data-model object schema. It is a notable result type within the coverage module.

A small React UI component that renders white-label or default branding (a logo plus a name) on the share page. It is a reusable presentational component with a size prop. It has minor architectural significance and only concerns the user interface.

A parameter-bag interface for a single query function, declaring four argument fields. It is an implementation detail of the function signature rather than a domain data shape a maintainer would name. Too fine-grained to be an architectural element.

A React component that renders the event-properties panel inside EventsPage. It composes select and combobox controls, charts and a pivot table, and binds them to a data query. It is a non-routable region of a parent view, so it is a subview, and a notable UI unit within the events screen.

Builds and issues an ad hoc SQL aggregation query against the website_event table via rawQuery. This is the relational (Prisma/Postgres) branch of a query-layer function, making it a data-store access pattern that reads durable storage. It is a notable but internal unit within the analytics query module.

DialogButton is a reusable UI component definition with a props schema (icon, label, title, sizing, open state) that wraps a button and modal dialog for use across many views. That makes it a UX library component. It is a notable shared building block, but it is not a core architectural element.

A TypeScript interface declaring only typed fields (the argument shape for the saveRevenue query) is an object schema per the data-model rules. It is a parameter DTO local to one query module, so its architectural significance is minor. It declares a shape and performs no persistence itself.

This is the relational (Prisma/SQL) variant of a query that reads the session_data and website_event tables to build an aggregated numeric time series. It is a named read operation issued from application code against the store, so it is a data-store access pattern of moderate significance.

A concrete UI button in Umami's goals report that opens a dialog containing the GoalEditForm to add a goal. It is a user-operable trigger control rather than a reusable library component, so it fits actioncomponent. It is a minor unit within the goals page, and its only concern is rendering UI.

A trivial React props interface with a single websiteId field for the WebsiteShareForm component. It is component boilerplate that a maintainer would not name as an architectural element on its own; the component itself would be the UX element.

IconLabel is a reusable presentational React component in common/, with a props schema (icon, label, weight) and 30 callers across views. It is a small UI building block in the shared component library, so it maps to ux.librarycomponent with low significance: a trivial layout primitive.

Next.js route module defining the GET /api/links/charts HTTP endpoint with a zod query contract. It filters the requested link IDs through canViewLink permission checks and delegates chart data retrieval to the query layer. This is an API operation, and it performs authorization filtering itself.

A React component props interface for WebsitesTable that extends DataTableProps with two optional fields. It is a component's property typing detail, part of the WebsitesTable component rather than an architectural element of its own. Props schemas are attributes of a UX library component, not separate nodes.

A trivial fallback rendering helper inside MetricLabel that wraps FilterLink with the data label. It is an implementation detail of the MetricLabel UI component, not something a maintainer would name as a separate architectural element, though it does render UI.

A TypeScript interface that only declares the shape of a query result row (name plus session metric counts). This makes it an object schema in the data-model layer. It is a minor result type local to one query module and does no I/O itself.

Small client-side module storing a post-login return URL in session storage and validating it to prevent open redirects. This is navigation state carried across route transitions, which fits a context variable. It is a minor utility; the open-redirect check is input validation, not authorization.

A props interface for the WorldMap React component. It is part of that component's definition rather than an architectural element of its own. It only declares optional websiteId and data inputs, extending ColumnProps, and has no logic or callers. Below modelling granularity.

This is a React UI component module that renders the realtime activity log on the website realtime page. It provides filter buttons, search and a virtualized list. It is a non-routable building block embedded in the realtime view, a notable UI unit in the realtime feature with no persistence or auth logic.

Internal click handler inside the CopyButton UI component. It writes to the clipboard and toggles transient 'copied' state with a timeout. This is an implementation detail of the component, not an architectural element on its own. It does drive UI state, so user_interface is marked.

Computes the rotating session salt (monthly, daily, weekly or fixed) that collection-session resolution uses to derive anonymised visitor session IDs. It is a configurable internal policy function that a maintainer would name when explaining session identity. It does not authenticate users or touch storage, so it fits best as an application function rather than security logic.

A small reusable UI component in common components that pairs an icon with an optional text label. It declares a props schema, so it is a library component definition. Its significance is low because it is a presentational primitive and has no callers recorded.

A small internal props/shape interface for positioning annotation markers on a chart. It holds only UI geometry and grouping and has no callers. It is an implementation detail of a chart component, not a domain data schema or an architectural UX element in its own right.

A small React hook module that supplies a reusable chart-bar click interaction. Clicking a bar zooms the date range by pushing updated URL params. It is a UI interaction recipe (trigger plus route-change feedback) shared by chart components. It is minor and local in significance.

Relational (Prisma/SQL) implementation of the getEventData query: issues paged and count SQL reads over website_event and event_data, filtered by website and date range. This is a named read access pattern issued from application code, not stored logic. It is one backend variant of a query module, so it is notable but not core.

A TypeScript interface declaring only named, typed fields for a chart annotation datum. Per the rules, a shape-only declaration is a data-model object schema. It is a minor UI-supporting type used within the chart markers component, so its significance is low. It renders nothing itself and implements no cross-cutting concern.
