A Next.js page-level component for a website's segments screen. It composes website controls and a segments data table inside a panel. It is a routable UI surface, so it is modelled as a UX view. The page is notable within its module but not a core architectural element.

Next.js route handler for DELETE /api/websites/{websiteId}/goals/{goalId}, which makes it an API operation. It delegates authentication to parseRequest, the permission check to canDeleteReport, and storage to deleteReport. It only orchestrates those calls, so the handler itself implements no cross-cutting concern.

A props interface for a React combo box component. It is the prop typing of a UI component, so it would be an attribute of the ux component's prop schema rather than a standalone architectural element. It is a minor implementation detail.

A shared React Query hook that assembles date, timezone and filter parameters into an analytics query and fetches website analytics via the API client. It is a reusable client-side data-fetching function. The HTTP call itself goes through useApi, so the hook does not own the integration. It is a notable but internal unit.

A TypeScript interface that only declares a shape (values array and total) for query result data. That makes it an object schema. It is a small result type with no callers, local to the getWebsiteListCharts query module, so its significance is minor. It does no persistence work itself.

A React form component for creating and editing funnel report definitions. It is rendered inside the Funnel view and the add-button modal, so it is a non-routable UI region composing form fields and step rows. It submits via an API mutation hook rather than calling the API itself.

Builds and executes an ad hoc ClickHouse SQL query over the website_event and website_event_stats_hourly tables to aggregate pageview metrics. It is a read access pattern issued from application code, and is the ClickHouse variant of a query-layer function, so it is a notable but not central unit.

A TypeScript interface declaring only named, typed fields (sum, count, average, unique_count, arpu) as the result shape of a revenue stats query. Per the spec, shape-only declarations are data-model object schemas. It is a minor result type local to one query module.

Umami query-layer function that dispatches a named read (active visitors for a website) to either the Prisma or the ClickHouse backend. It is a query-layer access pattern issued by application code against the session/event data. It is notable but not central.

React modal that opens a session profile when the session query param is set. Per the UX definitions a modal is a View. It gates visibility on share parameters, a light authorization check. It is a notable UI surface within the sessions area, though not core.

React component rendering a metrics bar region within the link detail page. It composes MetricsBar and MetricCard instances bound to website stats query data. It is a non-routable fragment of a specific view, so it is modelled as a subview. It is a notable but local UI unit.

This is an exported TypeScript interface that only declares the shape of the expanded event metric rows returned by a query (name, pageviews, visitors, visits, bounces, totaltime). A pure shape declaration is a data-model object schema. It is a minor result type that only its query module uses.

This is a React UI component that renders a table of Google Ads conversions per conversion action, with props websiteId and date range. It is a reusable component embedded in a Google Ads view rather than a routable page. It renders UI and delegates data fetching to a hook, so it does no persistence or integration itself.

A trivial one-line utility that converts an object's values into an array, equivalent to Object.values. It is a generic helper used by one UI component and has no architectural meaning of its own, so it is not modelled as an element.

A build-time tooling function that walks the Next.js API route files, uses the TypeScript compiler to analyse each exported HTTP method, and returns the discovered operations to the OpenAPI document builder. It is internal behaviour of the contract-generation module, not an API contract itself. It reads source files from disk.

A React component props interface for the Performance report view. It is a trivial prop-type declaration and part of the view's implementation. It is not a domain data shape and not a standalone architectural element, so it is captured implicitly by the ux view it parameterizes.

A React client component rendering the replay playback screen. It composes the player, session info and save form, adds keyboard navigation between replays, and handles save toggling. It is a distinct UI surface (a page or panel for one replay), so it is best modelled as a UX view of notable significance.

Inline error callback inside the two-factor setup modal that sets a localized error message in component state. It is a trivial handler and implementation detail of the modal view, not an architectural element on its own. Its only concern is driving the UI error display.

Type declaration of the error tracker collector's configuration: endpoint, enabled flag, release and environment tags, and a beforeSend hook. These set how error telemetry is exported to a backend, so it fits apm exporterconfig better than a plain data schema. As an ambient .d.ts interface with no callers, its significance is moderate.

Although the file is generated, it is the OpenAPI contract for POST /api/me/password (updateMyPassword): request body, responses and a bearer security requirement. That makes it the API operation element for the password-change endpoint. It declares auth but does not itself verify credentials or perform persistence.
